# Rollout Plan: Migration from Legacy Billing System to New Billing System

## Overview

This plan migrates 40,000 existing users from the legacy billing system ("Old") to the new billing system ("New"). Both systems will run in parallel (dual-run) for the duration of the migration, allowing rollback of any individual user or batch without service interruption. No decommissioning, disabling, or deletion of the old system occurs until a separate, dedicated decommission phase that starts only after the final migration batch has passed its full validation window.

---

## Phase Structure

### Phase 1: Canary (0.5% of users, ~200 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end reconciliation testing against a shadow copy of production data for 14 consecutive days with zero unresolved invoice/ledger mismatches, and rollback tooling (revert-to-old-system for a single user) has been tested successfully in staging.

**Population:** Internal accounts and opted-in low-risk external users (no active disputes, standard payment methods, monthly billing cycle only).

**Duration:** Minimum 7 days, covering at least one full billing cycle event (invoice generation) before proceeding.

### Phase 2: Early Adopters (10% of users, ~4,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed its full duration with zero critical incidents (see halt metrics below), invoice accuracy at 100% for canary cohort, and support ticket volume from canary users at or below baseline ticket rate for the equivalent cohort size.

**Population:** Randomly sampled users stratified across payment method types (card, ACH, invoice/net-terms) and billing frequencies (monthly, annual), excluding enterprise accounts with custom contracts.

**Duration:** Minimum 14 days, covering at least one full monthly billing cycle and one annual-billing edge case if present in the cohort.

### Phase 3: General Availability Ramp (40% of users, ~16,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 completed with cumulative invoice discrepancy rate below 0.1% (see halt metric), customer-reported billing complaints not exceeding 1.5x pre-migration baseline, and finance team sign-off on reconciliation reports for Phase 1 + 2 cohorts.

**Population:** Broad general user base, excluding highest-value enterprise/custom-contract accounts, which are held back for Phase 4.

**Duration:** Minimum 14 days, staged in two sub-batches of 20% each with a 3-day bake period between sub-batches to catch delayed billing-cycle issues.

### Phase 4: Full Migration Including Enterprise Accounts (49.5% of users, remaining ~19,800 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 fully complete with no open Severity-1/Severity-2 incidents attributable to the new billing system, dual-run reconciliation dashboards green for 7 consecutive days, and explicit written sign-off from Finance, Support, and Engineering leads.

**Population:** All remaining users, including enterprise accounts with custom contracts, migrated in contract-aware batches (custom pricing/terms validated individually before batch inclusion).

**Duration:** Minimum 21 days given contract complexity, with enterprise accounts migrated in the final sub-batch only after standard accounts in this phase are confirmed stable for 7 days.

### Phase 5: Old System Decommission (post-migration, 0% additional user migration)

**Entry criterion:** 100% of users successfully migrated and stable on the new system for a minimum of 30 consecutive days with zero open reconciliation discrepancies; full data archival of the old system completed and verified restorable; final audit sign-off from Finance and Compliance.

**Scope:** This phase performs no user migration. It is exclusively read-only freeze, archival, and eventual decommissioning of the old billing system, kept fully separate from the final user migration batch in Phase 4 per the hard requirement against combining decommissioning with the last migration batch.

---

## Halt Metrics (numeric thresholds)

The rollout must be immediately paused (no further batches promoted) if any of the following occur:

- **Invoice discrepancy rate exceeds 0.5%** of invoices generated in the new system within any rolling 24-hour window (compared against shadow-reconciled expected values).
- **Failed/duplicate payment charge rate exceeds 0.2%** of transactions processed in the new system within any rolling 24-hour window.
- **Customer-reported billing support tickets exceed 3x the pre-migration baseline rate** for the currently migrated cohort within any rolling 48-hour window.
- **Reconciliation job lag (old vs. new ledger sync) exceeds 4 hours** for more than two consecutive sync cycles.

Any single breach triggers an automatic freeze of further phase/batch promotion pending root-cause analysis; already-migrated users are not automatically rolled back unless the specific incident is user-impacting (e.g., incorrect charge), in which case affected users are individually reverted to the old system via dual-run failback.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or double-billing of users during the dual-run window due to both systems independently triggering invoice generation | Implement an idempotency lock and single source-of-truth flag per user account that designates exactly one system as authoritative for charge execution at any time, with the non-authoritative system running in shadow/read-only mode | Billing Platform Engineering Lead
RISK: Data drift between old and new systems for payment method tokens, causing failed charges after migration | Run automated reconciliation jobs every 4 hours comparing tokenized payment methods and account balances between systems, alerting on any mismatch before a user's cutover is finalized | Data Migration Engineering Lead
RISK: Enterprise customers with custom contract terms (discounts, proration rules, multi-entity billing) are migrated incorrectly, causing revenue leakage or customer disputes | Require manual contract-term validation and customer success sign-off for each enterprise account prior to inclusion in any migration batch, with enterprise accounts held to the final sub-batch of Phase 4 | Enterprise Customer Success Lead
RISK: Rollback path for a migrated user fails or is untested at scale, leaving no safe recovery option during an incident | Test single-user and batch-level rollback procedures in staging before each phase and re-verify rollback success criteria at the start of every phase using a small synthetic batch | Site Reliability Engineering Lead
RISK: Support and Finance teams are unable to triage new-system billing issues due to unfamiliarity with new tooling, slowing incident response | Conduct hands-on training and produce a runbook for Support/Finance before Phase 2 begins, and staff an on-call billing engineer during all active migration windows | Support Operations Lead

---

PHASES: 5
